reader_caveats: FINANCE LEASE RESOLVED: the Note 21 table headed 'as of June 30, 2024' (total liability 262,841) is the FY2023 table with its first row removed - the FY2023 audit shows the identical later rows (106,833; 88,679; 52,359; 14,970) under a total of 381,418 - so it was not updated for leases added in FY2024. The balance sheet (124,986 + 224,586 = 349,572), the financial responsibility schedule (349,572) and the 2024 comparative column of the FY2025 audit all agree, so 349,572 is the audited carrying amount; using the note table instead would lower the total by 86,731. The $3.9 million is captioned 'Note payable' on the balance sheet although Note 2 calls it a line of credit; if a reader treats the caption as decisive the total becomes $12,230,744. It was still outstanding a year later ($3,962,500 at 30 June 2025 per the FY2025 audit). Note 21 text describes the leases as office-equipment leases recognised on adopting ASC 842 and speaks of 'operating liabilities', while the balance sheet and the note table label them finance leases; the balance-sheet label is followed. Other internal inconsistencies in the scan: the liquidity note cites a line of credit 'totaling $2,500,000' while Note 2 says $5,000,000; the supplementary plant schedule shows 'Plant-related debt -0-'; the cash-flow statement labels the HBCU loan draw 'Repayment of federal capital contributions'. reader_caveats: COORDINATOR DECISION POINT: the added $1,087,510 rests on the stated-maturity limb of the rule alone; the College's own balance sheet presents the line as a current liability. The 26 August 2025 date is repeated unchanged in the FY2025 audit, so it is not a one-off misprint, but the FY2023 audit described the same line as renewed 3 June 2022 with a maturity of 30 August 2022. Notes payable: the note text gives due dates of 14 December 2024 and 5 May 2025, yet the maturity table and the balance sheet place $660,168/$660,169 beyond one year; balances are reported as printed. The $3,282,641 line had passed its renewed maturity (29 November 2024) without a new date by the report date. The financial responsibility schedule shows 'Long-term debt - for long-term purposes - Total 800,619', which does not agree with the balance-sheet notes payable (720,189) or with notes plus finance leases (740,599). Report dated 19 February 2025; compliance reports reissued 20 November 2025; FAC acceptance 13 December 2025.

entity_note: Florida Memorial University, Inc. (EIN 590668483; UEI C3B8EZBZSCP3).
reader_caveats: Re-checked on 2026-11-28; no FY2024 audited document or audited campus figure exists in any place searched, so no value is recorded. (1) Federal Audit Clearinghouse search form: by EIN 590668483 (8 submissions, audit years 2016-2023, none later); by UEI C3B8EZBZSCP3 (audit years 2022 and 2023 only); by name 'florida memorial' (same 8); by name 'florida memorial' restricted to audit years 2024 and 2025 ('No results found'); by name 'memorial' in Florida for audit years 2024-2025 (8 results, all hospitals or other organisations). The latest submission is audit year 2023, report 2023-06-GSAFAC-0000034387, accepted 1 April 2024. There is also no audit-year-2025 submission whose comparative column could supply 30 June 2024 figures. (2) Florida Auditor General: the Florida Single Audit Act e-file index lists other private universities (for example Bethune-Cookman and Lynn) but has no Florida Memorial entry; the other four index pages have none; direct report file names for 2023, 2024 and 2025 return 404. (3) University website (fmu.edu) site searches for 'financial statements' and 'audit': no financial statements posted. (4) Two web searches for the FY2024 audit: nothing. A FY2024 single audit would have been due 31 March 2025; its absence about twenty months later, is itself something a reader should know; so is the University's own accreditation status notice (PDF on fmu.edu, file dated 19 December 2025, which I read), stating that SACSCOC placed it on Probation for Good Cause for twelve months citing Standards 13.3 (Financial Responsibility), 13.4 (Control of Finances) and 13.6 (Federal and State Responsibilities). The Form 990 figure quoted by the first researcher is not an audited statement and is not used.
